title: False emergency start on path A: find the blown PT fuse
summary: Path A tripped off utility on ANSI 27 and the transfer controller started the generators: the path is now on generators. The utility company reports no outage. Find out why before you retransfer. In the control compartment of the MV transfer lineup (field view, CONTROL): with the multimeter on V AC, measure both sides of the utility sensing fuse F-1A on TB-1; pull the F-1A fuse holder and check the fuse with the resistance range; replace the fuse and put the holder back. Then retransfer to utility (open transition, MV transfer A in REMOTE) and stop the generator bus.
references: Operator master specification (digital twin EPMS), subsystem 2: CPT and draw-out fuse holders F-1A / F-1B; a blown F-1A leaves 0 V AC on the secondary with 27.5 kV on the primary and starts a false emergency transfer; TB-1 with a true-RMS multimeter on F-1A (120 V AC), P1-N1 (125 V DC), 73-74 and the 52TC / 52CC circuits
Model reading: F-1A also feeds the ANSI 27 element, so 52-U trips. Many relays supervise PT fuses (ANSI 60 loss of potential) and block 27 instead; this model has no 60 element
Fuse check practice: about 0 V across an intact fuse in circuit, about the supply voltage across a blown one; resistance only with the fuse out of circuit
Retransfer as DRILL-02: open transition, 52-U and 52-GM never closed together

steps.text: Measure F-1A line side to N on V AC (utility PT secondary: about 120 V)
Measure F-1A load side to N on V AC (0 V: the controller sees no utility)
Check the fuse on the resistance range (OL = open)
Replace the fuse and put the holder back
Retransfer to utility (MV transfer A in REMOTE: Retransfer to utility)
